Low bleeding risk, symptomatic/postrevascularization → low-dose rivaroxaban + aspirin; no full anticoagulation solely for PAD

rows.label: Complications
items: Gangrene, infection, amputation; MI/stroke often dominate long-term mortality
Reperfusion → compartment syndrome, hyperkalemia, rhabdomyolysis; irreversible limb may require primary amputation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Daily foot inspection**, protective footwear, diabetic foot care, BP/glucose control
Avoid thermal injury to insensate feet; antithrombotic plan after procedures based on bleeding risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Spinal stenosis: flexion relieves walking pain, pulses preserved
Venous ulcer: medial ankle, edema, pulses intact; neuropathy: sensory loss without ischemic pulse findings

table.title: Clinical stages
rows: Reproducible exercise pain relieved by rest
Buttock claudication, erectile dysfunction, weak femorals

polypharmacy-and-medication-reconciliati.name: Polypharmacy and medication reconciliation
polypharmacy-and-medication-reconciliati.scope: Polypharmacy in older adults, brown-bag medication review, Beers criteria, medication reconciliation across care transitions, deprescribing
polypharmacy-and-medication-reconciliati.core: Reconcile what the patient actually takes, then retain only drugs whose benefits fit current goals, risks, and time to benefit.

rows.label: Principle
items: Polypharmacy often defined as ≥5 drugs; count alone cannot establish prescribing quality
Older adults: altered clearance, frailty, cognitive impairment amplify interactions and adverse effects

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Brown-bag review**: prescriptions, OTCs, supplements, doses, actual use, indications, prescribers
★ Transitions: **compare home/inpatient/discharge lists**; resolve omissions, duplicates, changes
Assess renal dosing, interactions, adherence/cost; document changes and communicate one updated list

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid prescribing cascades: investigate new symptoms as possible drug effects before adding drugs
Do not continue hospital-only drugs without an outpatient indication

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ **Beers criteria flag risk**, not absolute bans; consider indication, alternatives, goals, preferences
Deprescribe highest harm/lowest benefit first; taper withdrawal-prone drugs, monitor symptoms
Limited life expectancy → reconsider preventive drugs with long time to benefit

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Do not abruptly stop benzodiazepines, opioids, or chronic steroids**; plan gradual reduction
Anticholinergics, sedatives, NSAIDs → confusion, falls, bleeding, renal injury
Recorded medication lists do not establish actual use

polypharmacy-and-medication-reconciliati.evidence: Not checked online; established geriatric medication reconciliation and Beers-based prescribing principles.

secondary-hypertension.name: Secondary hypertension
secondary-hypertension.scope: Renal artery stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing syndrome, coarctation of aorta, diagnostic workup
secondary-hypertension.core: Abrupt, unusually young, severe, or resistant hypertension suggests a treatable secondary driver.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atherosclerosis, fibromuscular dysplasia, renal disease, adrenal tumors, sleep apnea
NSAIDs, oral contraceptives, stimulants, glucocorticoids, licorice; medication nonadherence can mimic resistance

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hypokalemia** suggests mineralocorticoid excess but normal K does not exclude it
Flash pulmonary edema or creatinine rise >30% after ACE inhibitor/ARB → renovascular disease
Endocrine spells, cushingoid appearance, or upper-body hypertension guide cause-specific testing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Renal hypoperfusion activates RAAS; mineralocorticoid signaling increases distal sodium absorption and potassium loss
Catecholamine/cortisol excess, aortic obstruction, or nocturnal hypoxia increases vascular pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm **home/ambulatory BP**, adherence, cuff technique; BMP, urinalysis, creatinine, TSH
Sleep-apnea symptoms → polysomnography; abnormal urinary sediment → renal ultrasound and kidney evaluation
★ Biochemical testing precedes adrenal imaging; correct hypokalemia and account for interfering medications
Endocrine Society 2025: suggest **aldosterone screening for all hypertension**, conditional on resources

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Primary aldosteronism: unilateral → **adrenalectomy**; bilateral → spironolactone/eplerenone
Renovascular atherosclerosis → medical risk reduction; revascularize selected recurrent pulmonary edema or refractory disease
Fibromuscular dysplasia → angioplasty; critical bilateral renal stenosis → avoid ACE inhibitor/ARB
★ Pheochromocytoma: **alpha blockade before beta blockade**, volume expansion, then surgery
Treat cortisol source, repair significant coarctation, use CPAP for OSA; stop contributing drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, heart failure, CKD, retinopathy
Unopposed alpha stimulation after beta blockade can cause catecholamine crisis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor renal function/K after RAAS blockers or mineralocorticoid antagonists
Genetic evaluation/family screening for suspected hereditary pheochromocytoma or congenital aortic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: normal out-of-office readings
Essential hypertension: gradual course without specific endocrine/renal clues

table.title: Targeted workup
rows: Selective suppression test; CT/adrenal venous sampling
Plasma free or urine fractionated metanephrines

secondary-hypertension.evidence: Aldosterone screening checked 2026-10-30: [Endocrine Society 2025](https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/primary-aldosteronism-2); other causes: established teaching.

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal NAAT from exposed mucosal sites; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints usually need arthroscopic washout
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

shoulder-pain.name: Shoulder pain
shoulder-pain.scope: Rotator cuff tendinopathy and tear, impingement, adhesive capsulitis, dislocation, biceps tendinopathy, glenohumeral osteoarthritis
shoulder-pain.core: Active versus passive range of motion, true weakness, trauma history, and pain location distinguish major shoulder disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Overhead work/sports, repetitive lifting, aging; fall or traction → acute structural injury
Diabetes, thyroid disease, prolonged immobilization → capsular fibrosis
Seizure/electrocution → posterior dislocation; anterior instability follows abduction/external rotation injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Lateral upper-arm pain often shoulder origin; radiation below elbow suggests cervical source
Night pain with preserved passive motion suggests cuff disease; weakness persisting after analgesia suggests tear
★ **Fever, hot joint, severe pain with any motion** → urgent septic arthritis evaluation
★ Deformity, absent pulse, deltoid numbness → dislocation with possible neurovascular injury

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tendon degeneration/tearing impairs dynamic stabilization; capsule contracture restricts joint excursion
Loss of articular cartilage causes mechanically painful glenohumeral degeneration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs** for trauma, arthritis, deformity; include axillary or scapular-Y view for dislocation
Compare strength, provocative tests, neck examination; document axillary nerve and distal pulses
Ultrasound or MRI for suspected tear, persistent symptoms, or surgical planning; avoid routine immediate MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Most atraumatic disorders → **activity modification, NSAIDs, physical therapy**; maintain motion
Selected painful tendinopathy/capsulitis → corticosteroid injection; avoid repeated injections into tendons
★ Dislocation → **prompt closed reduction**, brief sling, rehabilitation; recheck neurovascular function afterward
Acute traumatic full-thickness tear with functional loss → early orthopedic referral; severe OA → arthroplasty consideration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent instability, axillary nerve injury, greater-tuberosity fracture, persistent weakness
Prolonged sling use → stiffness; chronic massive tear → cuff arthropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Rotator cuff/scapular strengthening, ergonomic changes, gradual return to overhead activity
Early supervised motion after injury when safe; avoid unnecessary immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervical radiculopathy: dermatomal symptoms, neck-provoked pain
ACS: exertional referred discomfort, diaphoresis, no motion-dependent localization
Pancoast tumor: smoking, hand weakness, Horner syndrome

table.title: Localizing examination
rows: Painful arc; positive Hawkins/Neer; strength preserved
Drop-arm or lag; objective resisted-movement weakness
Both active/passive motion limited, especially external rotation
Flattened deltoid; arm abducted, externally rotated
Anterior groove tenderness; pain with resisted supination

shoulder-pain.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAOS rotator cuff guideline 2025](https://www.aaos.org/quality/quality-programs/rotator-cuff/); other examination patterns established teaching.

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → shave, punch, or excisional biopsy deep enough to assess invasion
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform appearance

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

smoking-cessation.name: Smoking cessation
smoking-cessation.scope: Mortality reduction, 5 As counseling, pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement, bupropion, varenicline), behavioral programs
smoking-cessation.core: Stopping tobacco lowers cardiovascular, cancer, pulmonary, and all-cause mortality at any age; counseling plus drugs produces the best quit rates.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **Ask every adult** about tobacco, vaping, dependence, prior attempts; include pregnancy
No readiness to quit → motivational interviewing; connect personal goals to cessation benefits

rows.label: Start/stop
items: 5 As: **Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, Arrange**; agree quit date, identify triggers
Arrange early follow-up, behavioral program, quitline; relapse → reassess triggers and renew treatment

rows.label: Test
items: Cigarettes/day, time to first cigarette, withdrawal; no routine biochemical confirmation
Check pregnancy, renal function, seizure/eating-disorder history before selecting drugs

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Nonpregnant adults → **varenicline or combination nicotine replacement** plus behavioral support
Pregnancy → counseling first; if unsuccessful, discuss drugs individually, evidence uncertain

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Psychiatric history alone does not contraindicate varenicline; monitor mood changes
E-cigarettes: insufficient USPSTF evidence for cessation; avoid recommending during pregnancy
Stopping smoke exposure reverses CYP1A2 induction → ↑clozapine/theophylline; nicotine not responsible

table.title: Drug selection
rows: Nausea, vivid dreams; renal dose adjustment
Avoid seizures, eating disorders, abrupt alcohol withdrawal

somatic-symptom-disorders.name: Somatic symptom disorders
somatic-symptom-disorders.scope: Somatic symptom disorder, illness anxiety disorder, conversion disorder, factitious disorder, malingering, regular scheduled visits, validating suffering
somatic-symptom-disorders.core: Distressing symptoms or health fears require a positive psychiatric formulation, validation, and proportionate medical evaluation; intent separates factitious behavior from functional symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trauma, anxiety/depression, chronic illness, major stress; medical and psychiatric disorders can coexist

rows.label: Clues
items: Persistent reassurance seeking, repeated testing, high health-related distress, impaired function
Assess suicidality, abuse, substance use, and medication-related symptoms; avoid assumptions based on demographics

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Attention, threat appraisal, and learned responses amplify suffering; symptoms do not require conscious production
External reward differs from internal sick-role motivation; neither can be inferred from one inconsistency

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Somatic symptom disorder does not require medically unexplained symptoms**; excessive response is decisive
Illness anxiety requires ≥6 months preoccupation; somatic symptom persistence typically >6 months
★ Functional neurologic disorder: **positive incompatible examination signs**, such as Hoover sign, support diagnosis
New objective abnormalities still warrant targeted medical evaluation; avoid diagnosing solely by exhaustive exclusion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **One clinician, scheduled visits**, focused examinations; validate suffering without endorsing unproven disease
CBT, functional rehabilitation, treat comorbid anxiety/depression; explain functional neurologic mechanisms nonjudgmentally
★ Avoid repeated low-value procedures; **new red flags → reassess**, regardless of established psychiatric diagnosis
Factitious: coordinated team, factual records, supportive discussion; protect dependents from induced illness

rows.label: Complications
items: Iatrogenic injury, unnecessary surgery, opioid exposure, disability, fragmented care
Factitious disorder imposed on another → serious abuse risk requiring safeguarding action

rows.label: Mimics
items: Occult medical disease: evolving objective findings or coherent physiologic abnormalities
Delusional disorder: fixed somatic belief despite evidence, without flexible doubt

table.title: Distinguishing patterns
rows: Motor/sensory symptoms incompatible with neurologic disease
Intentional deception; no obvious external reward

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea may be an anginal equivalent
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
No routine repeated anatomic/stress testing in stable asymptomatic patients without functional change

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; negative nitrites do not exclude infection
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen; selected recurrences → postcoital/continuous antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, previous VTE, inherited thrombophilia

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Most stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

viral-hepatitis.name: Viral hepatitis
viral-hepatitis.scope: Hepatitis A, B, C, D, E, serologic markers, acute vs chronic hepatitis, HCV antibody and RNA confirmatory testing, direct-acting antivirals, postexposure prophylaxis (HBIG and vaccine)
viral-hepatitis.core: Hepatocellular injury with malaise, anorexia, jaundice, and high aminotransferases prompts exposure-based viral testing; chronic infection may be clinically silent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HAV/HEV: fecal–oral spread; HBV/HCV/HDV: blood, perinatal exposure; HBV also sexual
Injection exposure, unscreened blood, endemic birth region; HDV requires HBV
HEV severe in pregnancy; perinatal HBV and most untreated HCV often become chronic

rows.label: Clues
items: Dark urine, pale stool, RUQ discomfort; transaminases often far exceed alkaline phosphatase
★ **Encephalopathy + INR ≥1.5 without preexisting cirrhosis** → acute liver failure
HBV: serum sickness, polyarteritis nodosa; HCV: mixed cryoglobulinemia, porphyria cutanea tarda

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Host immune injury to infected hepatocytes; persistent HBV/HCV → fibrosis and carcinogenesis
HBV nuclear templates persist; HCV cure does not confer immunity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ HAV acute → **IgM anti-HAV**; total/IgG antibody indicates immunity
★ **HCV antibody → reflex HCV RNA**; antibody persists after clearance; recent exposure → RNA directly
HBsAg persisting >6 months → chronic HBV; HBV DNA quantifies replication
HEV testing by exposure/context; HBsAg-positive severe hepatitis → consider anti-HDV/HDV RNA
INR, bilirubin, creatinine; chronic disease → fibrosis staging, coinfection testing

rows.label: Tx
items: HAV, most HEV, uncomplicated acute HBV → supportive care; liver failure → urgent transplant center
★ Chronic HCV → **glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir**, usually 8–12 weeks; verify interactions/cirrhosis
Chronic HBV needing treatment → tenofovir or entecavir; severe acute HBV also may need antiviral
HCV cure: RNA undetectable ≥12 weeks after completion; do not delay treatment awaiting spontaneous resolution

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant hepatitis; chronic HBV/HCV → cirrhosis, portal hypertension, hepatocellular carcinoma
HBV can cause HCC without cirrhosis; DAAs may reactivate unrecognized HBV

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Susceptible HBV exposure → **HBIG + vaccine promptly**, preferably within 24 h; immunity determines exceptions
HAV exposure ≤2 weeks → vaccine; add immune globulin for immunocompromise/chronic liver disease
HAV/HBV vaccines, safer sex/injection practices; no HCV vaccine or proven HCV PEP
Cirrhosis/selected HBV → HCC surveillance with ultrasound ± AFP every 6 months

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced injury: medication/toxin relationship
Ischemic hepatitis: shock preceding abrupt marked aminotransferase rise
